The kids notice when I just…stop talking and stare at the board. If someone drops a book or a chair scrapes loudly, I jerk so hard it scares them—and me. Any sudden sound feels like it goes straight through my body.

I used to really enjoy being in the classroom and doing little projects with my students, but lately everything feels flat. Even at home with my husband, when he tries to plan something nice, I just can’t feel happy. I keep thinking that what happened was somehow my fault—that if I’d done something differently, maybe it wouldn’t have turned out the way it did. That thought is always there, and it makes me so irritable. I snap at him and at my coworkers over tiny things, like I’m carrying this low, constant anger I can’t shake.

Sometimes I hear what sounds like my name being called, or faint voices, usually when it’s quiet. I can’t always tell if it’s in my head or outside, and I don’t know what to make of it.
D018-D005_h001.question_a:
It really started about six months ago, after the car accident on the freeway. Since then it feels like that day is stuck to me. If I hear tires screech outside the classroom or even a loud bang from kids dropping books, my whole body just locks up. Sometimes I’m suddenly right back there—I can *hear* the crunch of metal and the screaming so clearly it’s like it’s happening again, even though I know I’m standing in my classroom. It’s not random; it’s always tied to something that reminds me of the crash.

I jump at every loud sound now. If a door slams, I physically flinch, sometimes to the point the kids notice. My concentration is awful—I’ll lose my place mid-sentence while teaching or reading a simple story to the class.

I feel like I can’t really feel happy anymore, even when I’m with my husband or my students. I go through the motions, but it’s flat. I keep thinking it’s my fault, that I should’ve seen the other car, done something different. Underneath everything, I’m just…angry—at myself, at other drivers, at anyone who seems careless. It’s like this simmering rage I can’t shake.
D018-D005_h001.question_b:
It’s been going on a little over a year now, maybe closer to a year and a half. Since the accident, anything that reminds me of it—sirens, screeching brakes on the street outside the school, even a scene in a movie—hits me really hard. My chest tightens, my heart races, and it’s like I’m back in that moment, thinking, “If I’d just looked twice, maybe it wouldn’t have happened.” I keep replaying it and blaming myself.

But it’s more than that. I’ve become… flat. I used to love my kids at school, loved planning lessons and silly crafts. Now I feel nothing, even when they run up to hug me or my husband tries to cheer me up. I’m just numb and oddly irritable; there’s this low boil of anger inside me that comes out over tiny things.

My concentration is awful. I lose my place while reading to the class, forget instructions mid-sentence. Loud noises in the hallway make me jump out of my skin. They don’t match the memories; they feel like something separate and wrong.

Sleep is rough. I keep having these bad dreams that wake me up in a panic. They’re not always clear when I wake up, but they have the same kind of feeling, like something terrible is about to happen or already happened. I wake up sweating, heart racing, and then I can’t get back to sleep.

Lately I’ve also been hearing things that I can’t tell are real or not—like a voice calling my name or saying something under its breath when no one’s around, especially when I’m out on late deliveries. Sometimes I think I see something out of the corner of my eye and when I look, nothing’s there.

I get irritated so fast now. I’ve snapped and shoved people, slammed doors, thrown stuff when I get overwhelmed. And even on days when I hit all my delivery targets or my boss compliments me, I just feel…nothing. No pride, no relief. Just the same heavy, scared feeling.
D018-D005_h022.question_a:
It started about six months ago, after that car crash on the highway when the other driver died. Since then, sleep has been a mess. I keep having these nightmares where I’m back in the truck, hearing the screeching brakes and seeing his face right before impact. Sometimes when a horn blares or a bike cuts in front of me on my route, it’s like I’m suddenly there again — for a few seconds I actually see the smashed windshield and smell the smoke, even though I know I’m really on a different street. It’s not random voices or anything; it’s always that accident replaying itself.

I feel on edge all the time, like something bad is about to happen. My shoulders are tight, I’m jumpy with any loud noise, and I can’t seem to relax, even on my days off. When something goes well at work — finishing all the deliveries early, getting good feedback — I just feel numb, like it doesn’t matter. I’ve snapped a few times too, shoved a coworker who startled me from behind, slammed doors, thrown my phone against the wall. I hate that I’m like this, but I can’t seem to control it.

What’s weird is that I also hear a man’s voice commenting on what I’m doing, like, “You’re messing this up,” or “They’re watching you,” even when I’m just loading packages. It doesn’t sound like the crash, and it’s not about the accident—it’s just there, out of nowhere, even when I’m not thinking about what happened.
